newsitem.title: USA: U.S. automotive execs concerned by Japan trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. automotive execs concerned by Japan trade.

text.p: Chief executives of U.S automobile industry supplier companies expressed concerns about trade trends with Japan in a letter to Commerce Secretary William Daley released on Thursday.

The Joint Automotive Supplier Council, comprising the chief executives of 36 companies that supply the U.S. automobile industry, said they were worried about the weakness of the yen and slow progress on deregulation as called for in a 1995 automotive trade agreement.

"The Japanese government appears to be backsliding on its commitments to deregulate its auto parts aftermarket, as evidenced by the recent rejection of the U.S. industry's petition to deregulate replacement brake parts," the letter said.

"Also, only 114 Japanese outlets for American-made cars and trucks have been announced, compared with the 200 anticipated when the agreement was signed, and only a handful of those are affiliated with Japan's leading automakers," it said.
The letter was signed by Lawrence Bossidy of AlliedSignal Inc and Robert Eaton of Chrysler Corp, who serve as co-chairmen of the council.
The Commerce Department and U.S. Trade Representative are due to release a review of the 1995 automotive trade agreement on Friday.
